approach: Add one pure reading check, `check_behavior_test_design`, in crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs. It is wired as one `step!` line directly after `check_code_survey` (checks.rs:539). It reads the `Code survey:` assumptions, `Existing code:` assumptions, criteria and deliverables, plus the schema tags compiled into athena-data's `AnyRecord` and `HistoryRecord`. It parses labelled clauses (`Entry point:`, `Gate order:`, `Stop gate:`, `Reuses:` with `Existing code:` accepted as an alias, `Output:`, `Direct check:`) and judges each clause alone. (a) Entry point and gate order hold identifiers, and the stop gate is one of the gate-order identifiers. (b) Reuse names an identifier or says "no existing function". (c) `Output:` says no new output, names an accepted record kind (a tag, `AnyRecord::<Variant>`, `HistoryRecord::<Variant>` or `check_record_file`), or names a round-trip token that a criterion names with a deliverable that can hold the test. (d) Each non-routine behavior criterion has its own `Direct check:` clause. The clause cites that criterion's position among all criteria and holds a measurement verb. It names the entry point, a gate from the order, or a planner, producer or model call. It does not measure through a skip switch (phrase, identifier form such as `skip_probe`, or all-caps environment variable such as `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`) or through a read of an internal helper. A routine criterion that only says fmt, clippy and test pass or existing tests pass needs no clause. The refusal error names the check, so the line printed by `athena check-reading` names it (`check_reading_text` drops the step name, replay.rs:57-63). Revision-only changes: (1) verify.rs is a listed deliverable, visibility change only. (2) `athena check-reading` (`check_reading_command`, main.rs:687-715) and its tests are listed dependents, with one added CLI case. (3) The producer is told what to do when the in-loop replay reports a share above the limit. (4) Skip-switch matching covers identifier and environment-variable forms, and a Direct check must name the entry point, a gate or a model call. (5) Routine criteria are exempt. (6) The tag probe is kept and a `SCHEMA_TAGS` constant in athena-data is noted as a follow-up in the doc comment and CHANGELOG only. The guide `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` is rewritten in place to teach the labels with one filled-in example, and `survey_example()` extracts that example so the guide, both error texts and the tests share one source.

decisions.choice: Judge the survey by labelled clauses, not by whole-text phrase search. A clause runs from its label (case-insensitive, at the start of the text or after whitespace or a full stop) to the next label. A repeated label, or a label in a second `Code survey:` assumption, adds to the same clause. Labels are found on an ASCII-lowercase copy of the whitespace-normalised text, so identifier case (`AnyRecord`, `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`) is kept.
decisions.reason: The reading is a plain Vec<String> of assumptions (surveys.rs:117-124), so labels are the only structure available without changing the Reading type. Each part is read inside its own clause, so 'directly' or 'calls' in a description of the code cannot stand for a measurement, and a stop gate is looked up only in the `Gate order:` clause. The request lists five labels (Entry point, Gate order, Stop gate, Reuses, Direct check). The sixth, `Output:`, is added because (c) must be required in every reading: without a clause, 'omits exactly one of (a)-(d)' could not be told apart.

rejected.option: Whole-survey phrase search
rejected.why: A name in the list of paths read would pass as a stop gate, and 'directly' plus 'calls' anywhere would satisfy (d) for every criterion.

rejected.option: Typed fields on the Reading for the four parts
rejected.why: Changes the reading schema in athena-data and the reader prompt, out of scope (reader prompt has 2 tokens of headroom).

The check reads reuse text from a `Reuses:` clause, an `Existing code:` clause inside the survey, and every assumption returned by the existing `existing_code_assumptions(reading)` (surveys.rs:1329), taking the text after its label. (b) holds when the combined text has an identifier or the phrase 'no existing function'. Partial reuse ('`names_record_evidence`; no existing function checks gate order') is accepted.

The repository already reads an `Existing code:` assumption that lists reused functions (check_design_existing_code, surveys.rs:1409), and the kept plan's finding was that a reader who writes it that way must not be refused. Both forms satisfy (b), so there is one fact and no parallel list. `names_existing_path` is not used because (b) needs a function name.

decisions.choice: (a): `Entry point:` holds an identifier. `Gate order:` holds at least two distinct identifiers. `Stop gate:` holds an identifier equal, after trimming backticks and `()`, to one in the gate order. An identifier is a backtick-quoted token with no whitespace, or a bare whitespace token (trailing punctuation trimmed) containing `_` or `::` or ending in `()`. A prose stop gate is refused as missing (a). A stop gate not in the order is refused as a contradiction.
decisions.reason: Single-word functions such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) count when backticked. Bare prose words are not identifiers, so 'the resolution step' names no gate.

rejected.why: Refuses real single-word functions and the template.

rejected.option: Accept a prose stop gate
rejected.why: The check cannot compare prose with the order.

decisions.choice: (c): validate record kinds against the code. `accepted_record_tags()` deserialises `{"schema":"athena.probe-unknown/0"}` once as `athena_data::records::AnyRecord` and once as `athena_data::history::HistoryRecord` (both `#[serde(tag = "schema")]`; records.rs:1121-1199, history.rs:391-413; both modules pub), parses the backtick-quoted names after 'expected one of' in each serde error, and caches the union in a `OnceLock`. `record_kind_problem(output_clause)` checks: every `athena.<kind>/<n>` token is in the union; every `AnyRecord::<Variant>` or `HistoryRecord::<Variant>` maps (lowercased, hyphens removed, version suffix handled) to a tag of that enum; `check_record_file` is accepted. The clause passes on 'no new output' or 'no new record' with no record or data deliverable, on a valid kind, or on a round-trip token (`is_round_trip_token`, extracted from `names_record_evidence` with no behaviour change) that a behavior criterion also names with a deliverable that can hold the test (a `tests/` path, a path ending `records.rs`, or a path in the Output clause). A bare `AnyRecord` with no variant and no tag is refused ('names AnyRecord but no record kind'). 'No new output' beside a deliverable that satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable` is a contradiction. The step still calls `names_record_evidence` first. The doc comment says `check_record_file` accepts AnyRecord kinds only and history records are accepted by the history checks; it also names a follow-up: a pub `SCHEMA_TAGS` constant in athena-data next to `schema()` (records.rs:1407, history.rs:417) would remove the dependence on serde's message. The constant is not added now.
decisions.reason: `AnyRecord::schema` and `HistoryRecord::schema` need a value of the type and cannot list the tags, and editing athena-data is out of scope and would trigger the record-evidence rule. The probe reaches the real accepted kinds from athena-core. The pin test `accepted_record_tags_come_from_the_enums` reads records.rs and history.rs by `include_str!`, parses each `#[serde(rename = "athena.…")]` line and the variant line after it, and asserts the probed set equals the renamed set, `variant_tag` agrees for every parsed variant of both enums, a made-up variant maps to nothing, and both enums contribute tags. A serde message change fails a test, not a reading.

rejected.why: Passes 'athena.madeup/1' and a kind-less 'AnyRecord'.

rejected.option: Probe only AnyRecord
rejected.why: Refuses real history tags such as `athena.landing/1`.

rejected.why: Out of scope; follow-up only.

decisions.choice: (d) per-criterion direct checks. Criterion N in `Direct check: criterion N ...` is the 1-based position among ALL acceptance_criteria. Only non-routine criteria with `kind == Behavior` need a clause. A clause cites exactly one number; a clause with no number counts for the single non-routine behavior criterion only when there is exactly one. A clause citing several numbers (a list or a range, every number counted) is refused with 'one direct check covers N criteria; write one Direct check clause per criterion'. Each clause holds a measurement verb (`count`, `counts`, `counting`, `counted`, `asserts`, `asserting`, `compares`, `observes`). Uncovered numbers are listed in the error.
decisions.reason: The request asks for a direct check per property, and the reading's numbers are what the verifier sees. A fixture with two content criteria before the behavior criterion shows the number is the position (3), not the rank among behavior criteria. The doc comment says a clause can state an untrue measurement and the critic and verifier judge that.

rejected.option: Number only behavior criteria
rejected.why: Does not match the numbers shown in the reading.

rejected.option: Allow up to two criteria per clause
rejected.why: An arbitrary number.

decisions.choice: Routine criteria are exempt from (d) (finding 5). A new `is_routine_criterion(text)` in surveys.rs is true when every word from `clause_words` is in a small fixed list (cargo, fmt, clippy, test, tests, check, pass, passes, and, the, on, final, tree, existing, still, all, a, recorded, athena, same, locked, targets, d, warnings, workspace, no, unrelated, behavior, change, changes, build, clean, green, as, is, are, with, run) or a number, and the text holds one of fmt, clippy, test or tests and one of pass, passes, clean or green. A criterion that adds any other word (a new property) is not routine. An exempt criterion needs no clause. A reading whose behavior criteria are all routine needs no Direct check. No existing matcher exists (Grep of reading.rs and reading/ for fmt, clippy and 'existing tests' found none), so this is new and small.
decisions.reason: A regression criterion of the form 'cargo X passes' claims no new property, so 'criterion 9 asserts cargo test passes' would be ritual text and would add refusals. The word list is closed, so 'cargo test passes and the greeting prints hello' is not exempt. The accepted reading's criterion 9 text ('No unrelated behavior changes: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy and cargo test pass on the final tree, as a recorded Athena check on the same tree') is exempt; a fixture shows it.

rejected.option: Keep the rule and show the form in the guide
rejected.why: Ritual text and extra replay refusals.

rejected.option: Exempt any criterion that mentions cargo
rejected.why: 'cargo test passes and a new flag is honoured' would escape.

decisions.choice: Skip-switch and internal-helper contradictions, scoped to the means of measurement, built on the existing verify.rs helpers. `split_clauses`, `clause_words` and `is_negator` in verify.rs (1337, 1368, 1378) become `pub(crate)`, visibility only. `without` and `instead` are added as negators in a local wrapper `is_means_negator` in surveys.rs, not in `NEGATORS`. Segments are the `split_clauses` pieces further split at the word `but`; the raw segment keeps case for identifier tests. Phrase forms on `clause_words` windows: `skip switch`, `skip flag`, `skip option`, `test only switch`, `internal helper`, `private helper`. Identifier forms (finding 4), tested on raw tokens of a segment: a token that is an all-caps environment-variable name (uppercase letters, digits, `_`, at least one `_`, at least 4 characters, an optional `=value` suffix trimmed); or a lowercase identifier or `--flag` with a segment (split on `_` and `-`) equal to `skip`, `skipped`, `no`, `disable`, `disabled` or `bypass`, or starting with `skip`, `disable` or `bypass`. In a `Direct check:` clause a phrase or identifier counts unless a negator stands earlier in the SAME segment; a refusal verb within two words right before a phrase ('refuses a skip switch') also cancels, but refusal words elsewhere do not. In a behavior criterion only the phrase forms count, and only when a means phrase (`through`, `via`, `using`, `by reading`, `by inspecting`, `measured`, `checked`, `verified` or `tested` followed by `by` or `with`) is within 4 words before it in the same segment and no negator precedes it there. A bare `read` is not a means phrase.
decisions.reason: One splitter and one negator list for the repository's clause checks, not a third copy. Identifier forms close the gap the critic found: `clause_words` keeps `_` inside words, so `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` never match the phrase list. A single early `not` or `refused` no longer disables the check for the whole clause. Stated limits, in the doc comment and the CHANGELOG: matching is lexical; an identifier with a `no` segment such as `no_change_reason` is refused unless negated and must be reworded; a skip switch given a name with none of these segments is not caught; a criterion that describes a refusal fixture with 'through a skip switch' is refused and must be reworded.

rejected.option: A fresh `segments` function and negator list in surveys.rs
rejected.why: Near-duplicates verify.rs:1261-1380.

rejected.option: Add `without` and `instead` to verify.rs NEGATORS
rejected.why: Changes which verifier-prompt lines count as negated (check_verifier_prompt), a behavior change outside this job.

decisions.choice: Structural subject rule for `Direct check:` (finding 4): each clause must name the entry point (an identifier from `Entry point:`), a gate identifier from `Gate order:`, or a planner, producer or model call (the words planner, producer or model with call or calls). A clause that names none is refused as (d) ('names no entry point, gate or model call'). The doc comment states that a clause may also name other identifiers and that reading a reused helper beside a gate is caught only by the phrase and identifier forms.
decisions.reason: A clause such as 'criterion 2 asserts `names_record_evidence` returns true' has a measurement verb and no listed phrase, and is the internal-helper read the introspections describe. The structural rule uses labels the check already parses and adds no new label.

decisions.choice: The fixture replay test builds each case so every later check accepts it. For each case the new step refuses, assert the same reading with the complete survey is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The limit is read from `replay_limit_percent(Some(30))`, not hard-coded.

decisions.choice: Do not weaken the check to meet the replay limit (findings 3). The declared share is 'expected 30% of newly refused readings', with the 'because' sentence the reading already carries (replay.rs:170-186 accepts a share above 25 with a reason). The in-loop replay (`loop_replay`, run/mod.rs:2294, calling `replay_cases` at 2316) measures the real share on the host's records during the producer run and sends the share and job ids back. If it reports a share above the declared share plus 5 points (35), the producer does NOT loosen the labels, markers, phrase lists or exemptions. It finishes the change, states the measured share and the newly refused job ids in its report, and does not change the check to fit. If the feedback cannot be acted on without loosening, it stops with `no_change: blocked` and the share and ids as the detail.
decisions.reason: The earlier plan said no step can measure the share; the in-loop replay does, and the producer needs a rule for its result. The replay already holds a declared share plus 5 points (replay.rs:159-165, 289-308), so a person sees the number and decides.

steps: Step 1, athena-context briefs/reader.rs (first, so the example exists): rewrite `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` (line 356). Keep the opening ('Before you give behavior criteria for a code or tests change, read the code and write one assumption that starts with `Code survey:` and names the crates/ paths you read'). Replace the unlabelled list with the labelled parts: `Entry point:`, `Gate order:` (the order the run passes its gates, as identifiers), `Stop gate:` (the gate the test stops at, one of those), `Reuses:` (existing functions reused, or 'no existing function does X'; an `Existing code:` assumption also counts), `Output:` (no new output, or a record kind the records check accepts: a schema tag such as `athena.failure-class/1`, `AnyRecord::<Variant>` or `check_record_file`, or a typed record with a round-trip test listed as a deliverable), `Direct check:` (one clause per non-routine behavior criterion, citing its number as its position among all criteria, naming the entry point, a gate or a model call and what it counts or compares; never a skip switch, a skip or env-var name, or an internal-helper read; a criterion that only says fmt, clippy and test pass needs none; do not paste the example). End with the single line `Example survey: Code survey: crates/foo/src/run.rs. Entry point: `run_job`. Gate order: `resolve`, `probe`, `report`. Stop gate: `probe`. Reuses: `shared_helper`; no existing function checks gate order. Output: no new output. risks.risk: Skip-switch matching by identifier form is lexical: an identifier with a `no` segment such as `no_change_reason`, or an all-caps token, is refused in a Direct check unless negated (false positive); a skip switch whose name has none of the listed segments is not caught (false negative).
risks.mitigation: The doc comment and CHANGELOG state both limits; the error says to reword or negate. The structural rule (a Direct check must name the entry point, a gate or a model call) catches a clause that measures only a helper. The plan critic and verifier judge the rest.

Refused with `check_behavior_test_design`: a stop gate not in the order; a record or data deliverable beside 'Output: no new output'; `athena.madeup/1`; `AnyRecord::Nonsense`; a bare `AnyRecord`; a typed record with no round-trip token and no tag; a round-trip token no criterion names; a round-trip token with no deliverable under tests/, no records.rs and no path in the Output clause; a Direct check that measures 'through a skip switch'; 'criterion 2 asserts the reading is refused, measured through a skip switch'; identifiers `skip_probe`, `disable_probe`, `--no-probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE=1` in a Direct check; a criterion that checks 'by reading an internal helper'; a Direct check that asserts `names_record_evidence` returns true and names no entry point, gate or model call. Accepted twins: `athena.failure-class/1`; `athena.landing/1` (a HistoryRecord tag); `AnyRecord::FailureClass`; `AnyRecord::Candidate2`; `HistoryRecord::LandingIntent`; `check_record_file`; 'not a skip switch or a read of an internal helper'; 'not `skip_probe`' and 'without ATHENA_NO_PROBE'; the request's wording 'counting planner, producer or model calls, not reads of an internal helper and not a skip switch added just for the test'; this job's criterion 3 text; the guide example. `accepted_record_tags_come_from_the_enums` compares the probed set and the variant mapping with the rename and variant lines parsed from records.rs and history.rs. Corpus refusing ids: `design-stop-gate-not-in-order`, `design-new-typed-record-without-roundtrip-deliverable`, `design-typed-record-roundtrip-without-test-file`, `design-record-deliverable-beside-no-new-output`, `design-criterion-uses-skip-switch`, `design-criterion-reads-internal-helper`, `design-refusal-word-does-not-cancel-skip-switch`, `design-unknown-schema-tag`, `design-bare-anyrecord-no-kind`, `design-skip-identifier-direct-check`, `design-env-var-direct-check`. Accepting ids: `design-negated-skip-switch-accepted`, `design-negated-skip-identifier-accepted`, `design-request-wording-accepted`, `design-template-verbatim-accepted`, `design-known-schema-tag-accepted`, `design-history-schema-tag-accepted`, `design-anyrecord-variant-accepted`.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core design_check_contradiction && cargo test -p athena-core accepted_record_tags && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: Each contradiction is refused and named in the error; each twin is accepted; the tag pin test passes against the enum source.

A version that accepts any tag or bare `AnyRecord` fails the unknown-tag and bare-kind fixtures; one that probes only AnyRecord fails the `athena.landing/1` twin; one that checks phrases only fails the `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` fixtures; one that refuses on any mention, or lets a refusal word cancel, fails the accepted twins or the refusal-word fixture.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests `design_check_routine_criteria_need_no_direct_check` and corpus case `design-routine-criterion-accepted` build a complete reading (survey with all parts and a Direct check for criterion 1) plus a second behavior criterion, once with each routine text: 'cargo fmt, clippy and test pass', 'existing tests pass', and the accepted reading's criterion 9 text. With no clause for the routine criterion the reading is accepted. A twin with 'cargo test passes and the greeting prints hello' as the second criterion and no clause for it is refused, naming its number. A reading whose only behavior criterion is routine is accepted with no Direct check at all.
demonstrations.observes: Routine criteria are accepted without a clause; a criterion with an added property is refused as uncovered.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the exemption the routine readings are refused as (d) uncovered. With an exemption that matches any criterion naming cargo, the 'prints hello' twin is accepted and its test fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry `check_behavior_test_design` and `refusing_check`. `is_routine_criterion` is added by step 3 (no existing matcher found). Fixtures from `code_reading`; no double.

demonstrations.method: `design_check_replay_share_is_within_the_declared_range` builds 10 `ReplayCase` values with the existing `replay_case` helper and `base_checker` pattern (reading.rs ~6466-6545, exist): 3 code readings with the old short survey (newly refused), 3 with the complete survey, 4 docs readings, each built so every later check accepts it. Base checker and candidate checker both call `check_reading_text`; the base is applied to the reading with `FULL_SURVEY` swapped in, the candidate to the reading as built. For each newly refused case it asserts the swapped reading is accepted by `check_reading_text`. The declaration comes from `replay_declaration_of` on a reading whose criterion reads 'expected 30% of newly refused readings, because the check now asks for new required labels that past readings never used'. It asserts `!run.held`, at least 1 newly refused, and `newly_refused * 100 <= total * replay_limit_percent(Some(30))`. A second run whose candidate refuses every code reading asserts `run.held`. The real share is measured by the in-loop replay on the host records during the producer run (`loop_replay`, run/mod.rs:2294-2334); if it is above 35 the producer does not loosen the check and reports the measured share and newly refused job ids (decision on replay limit).
demonstrations.observes: The fixture share is within 30 plus 5 points, the held case holds, at least one case is newly refused, and the swapped readings are accepted by every other check.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check newly refused more than the limit of the fixtures, `run.held` is true and the assertion fails. If it refused nothing, the 'at least 1' assertion fails. A refusal that is not new (another check refuses the swapped reading) fails the swapped-reading assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entries `replay`, `replay_declaration_of`, `replay_limit_percent` and `check_reading_text` (replay.rs:54, 289-308, 365; exist). `ReplayCase` values and closures use the existing `replay_case` helper; the test is added by step 8. The closures only call `check_reading_text`; the logic under test is the production check. This test proves the arithmetic only: no independent expected share exists for the real records.

demonstrations.method: The existing tests `check_reading_prints_accept_for_a_reading_the_rules_accept` (main.rs:1277) and its neighbours still pass, because their fixture reading has class 'feature'. It asserts exit code 2, a line starting `refuse: ` with no newline, and the line contains `check_behavior_test_design` and `Gate order:`. A twin with the complete guide-example survey in the same helper asserts `accept` and exit 0, in a reading whose deliverable path is not checked (`check_reading_text` passes `repo_files = None`).
demonstrations.observes: Accept for the feature fixture, `refuse:` naming the new check for the short survey, `accept` for the complete survey.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the short-survey reading is accepted and the new test fails on the exit code.
